expectations.text: Identifies Ireland, Spain and France as the member states still lacking in-force transposition laws as of early September 2026
expectations.evidence: That leaves Ireland, Spain, and France — the three jurisdictions where you have subsidiaries — as still lacking in-force national transposition

expectations.text: Cites the July 9, 2026 Commission referral to the CJEU for failure to notify transposition — which originally also included the Netherlands
expectations.evidence: on 9 July 2026 the European Commission referred Ireland, Spain, France, and the Netherlands to the CJEU for failing to notify transposition of NIS2

expectations.text: Notes the Commission requested financial penalties: a lump sum plus daily penalty payments
expectations.evidence: seeking a lump-sum penalty plus daily fines

expectations.text: Notes the Netherlands has since transposed (Cbw in force August 15, 2026) and should no longer be listed as a laggard
expectations.evidence: the Netherlands has since transposed — its Cyberbeveiligingswet (Cbw)... entered into force on 15 August 2026, replacing the prior Wbni

expectations.text: Gives the right advice: prepare subsidiaries against the directive text now — authorities have applied short compliance windows once national law lands
expectations.evidence: Build to the directive text now... historical practice... has been to apply short or no compliance windows — the Netherlands' Cbw is the most recent example, with zero transition period
